entry.name: Jelly Cube
entry.description: A soft, deformable cube that jiggles when touched. VR-enabled with physics parameter controls for stiffness, damping, and pressure.
entry.qfep_connection: Low stiffness = high Î» territory. Form becomes fluid, resists fixed categories.

dna.default: assay=none - the early return in _assay_dressing, which does not even create the Assay pivot, so the 0.3 m soft body, its plinth, its label and its rack stand on nothing exactly as they did in all 4 rooms. Every other rung builds under ONE Node3D appended AFTER _create_vr_controls, so no legacy child index moves and no branch below the match touches _soft_body, _material or a single physics value. All four placements (SoftBodies_Soft_Body_Deformation and its _p1/_p2/_p3 siblings) are the bare token `jelly_cube:0:0.5:1` with no #key:value, and GridInteractablesComponent only calls apply_grid_config when merged_config is non-empty, so none of them reaches the new code at all.
dna.was: DERIVED, not composed. The axis, its allow-list, the five builders and the guarded apply_grid_config were already in commons/artifacts/jelly_cube/jelly_cube.gd (committed d3b41fbab) and the registry had never been told, so check_dna_declarations listed jelly_cube under 'promoted in code, undeclared in the registry' and the sweep could not reach any of it. What this pass added is the declaration and nothing else - not one line of the artifact was touched, because the code was already right: apply_grid_config returns unless the word is in the allow-list AND differs from the word already standing AND is_node_ready(), and _read_dna_meta lets a token's word be built once in _ready instead of built and torn down a frame later.
dna.note: assay is the softbody bench family's word and its five values, character for character - grab_jelly_bench, mass_spring_bench, energy_landscape_bench, membrane_bench, rigidity_dial_bench, abject_bench, octopus_bench, becoming_bench and tentacle_grab_bench all ask what apparatus a specimen is surrounded by, and jelly_cube stands in the same softbodies sequence as every one of them. The kit is re-dimensioned by a single factor u = cube_size / 0.5 so the family's proportions, accents and captions survive at this artifact's smaller scale; `control` is the rung that argues hardest, because an empty wire cage at the size the cube had BEFORE anything happened to it turns a thing you are watching into a difference you could disagree with.
dna.still_note: THE JIGGLE IS NOT AN AXIS AND CANNOT BE, and this is why the apparatus carries the claim instead. Everything jelly_cube exposes - stiffness, damping, pressure, mass - is a STARTING CONDITION on a body that relaxes, so five cubes started five ways settle into the same shape and photograph as one object five times; cloth_straps hit exactly this and took `suspension` for the same reason. Every assay rung is standing geometry: a graduated column, a wire reference cage, a plotted board, a glass case. The chart's settling trace is CLOSED FORM (exp(-3.4f)cos(13f)) and not sampled from the running solver, because a plot that came out different every launch would be noise wearing the costume of a record.
dna.framing_note: unchecked against a capture in this pass. The subject is a 0.3 m cube on a 0.42 m plinth, and _create_vr_controls already hangs a rack panel at z = 0.36 tilted -30 degrees; `chart` adds a board behind at -0.31 and `control` a second plate 0.35 m to the right, so the union-of-variants camera is pulled well back from the jelly itself. If the axis measures faint, check subject % before believing it - the apparatus IS the axis here, so a frame dominated by apparatus is not the failure it would be elsewhere.
dna.sibling_note: jelly_variants.gd carries the same axis and is likewise undeclared in the registry; it was outside this pass's three tokens and is left for the batch that owns it.

dna.was: one deep-red portal and only one - a top bar on two side posts with an open bottom, hard-coded in setup_frame(). A doorway, which is a claim: that the cloth is a threshold with a here and a there and that the point is to pass between them.
dna.note: the word and its five values are spring_system.suspension reused character for character - same question (what does a hanging body hang from, built to meet a rank that never moves), same four shapes plus none. NOT `support` (that axis is what a thing stands ON; nothing here stands on anything) and NOT `hang` (gallery_winner_showcase's axis is the arrangement of the hung objects; this one leaves the strap rank exactly where it was). strap_count is the @identity's critical_parameter and is deliberately NOT declared: with five suspension values the gallery's cap of 9 drops any second axis before it renders, so declaring it would add a ledger row no sweep ever measures. entry.name: Cloth Straps
entry.description: Hanging soft body cloth straps that the player can walk through.

dna.argues: Four identical SoftBody3D spheres fall from drop_height onto whatever is beneath them, and what is beneath them is nothing this artifact owns. `landing` gives each cell of the 2x2 grid a surface to negotiate with, so the four resting crumples differ because the MATERIAL met a different shape, not because a clock read differently. That is the softbodies truth line at its most literal: form is not imposed, it is what is left after a falling body and a rigid obstruction finish arguing. The @identity calls the four bodies 'one event, sampled four times'; this keeps that reading and changes what the event is falling INTO, which is the only part of it a photograph can hold.
dna.still_note: floor: a squashed ball, wide contact patch - the shipped picture. pan: the sphere is pinched between two tray walls 0.70 m apart and rises, taller than wide, with two flat vertical facets; the only value where the body ends up TALLER than it started. rail: a saddle, two lobes hanging either side of a 1.6 m bar with a crease along the top. cone: a tent, the lowest point pushed up into the body's own volume, dimpling the pressure-inflated shell. Four silhouettes that differ in ASPECT RATIO, not in arrival time. Each one is where the body stops, and each stays there - which is the whole requirement in a sequence made of motion: a stiffer cloth HANGS differently and that is a still, a cloth that reaches the same drape twice as fast is invisible.
dna.default: landing=floor. _build_landing() returns before constructing anything, so the child order stays exactly SoftBody_1..4 (each the instanced softbodybody.tscn) then StopTimer_1..4, and _build_bench_floor() returns on the same kind of guard. TWELVE appearances, none of them reached. FIVE bare grid tokens - SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics, _p1, _p2, _p3 and Corridor_SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics - with no rotation, no offset and no #key, so merged_config is empty and GridInteractablesComponent never calls apply_grid_config on them at all. SIX exhibit_furniture#kind:platform#size:l#mount:softstopscene slots (Trial_castelvecchio / grande / kanazawa / sainsbury / uffizi / wfc_softbodies), and exhibit_furniture._mount_artifact() instantiates the scene and add_child()s it with NO config call whatsoever - read, not assumed. ONE curation_station roster (Curation_Bay_softbodies_2, artifacts:gridagent,softmill,softstopscene), and curation_station calls inst.apply_grid_config({"emissive": false}) on everything it curates - a key this artifact does not read, so the signature is unchanged and it returns before touching the tree. The three fixture exports are no-ops at default too: drop_height 3.0 IS the literal 3 that used to be written in the positions array and 3.0 is exactly representable; bench_floor_y -1000.0 fails the `> -999.0` guard so no plane is built; body_damping -1.0 fails the `>= 0.0` guard so damping_coefficient is never written and each body keeps softbody3d.gd's own 0.01. This token lives in physics_simulation.json ONLY - no second registry to mirror.
dna.was: Four spheres released at y=3 over whatever the room happened to put under them, and four Timers that freeze them at 7.5 / 11 / 12 / 12 seconds. The artifact's argument was entirely in the CLOCK: the landing surface was never part of the composition, so the four crumples differed only in how long each body had been falling.
dna.note: NEW word. Not `bed` and not `ground` - both taken, and both are about what a thing is displayed ON, not what deforms it. Not `assay`, which four artifacts in this sequence already hold (jelly_cube, softmill, revolving_joy_ride, softbody_gallery_part2): assay is the apparatus word, and this builds no gauge, no chart, no vitrine and no wire cage, and adds nothing the player reads a number off. Not `repose` or `settling` (taken elsewhere, and both name the PROCESS this axis refuses to be about). The four values are load-bearing collision geometry and nothing else: one shared grey material across all of them on purpose, so the critic cannot score a paint job.
dna.declined: `stop_times` ([7.5, 11.0, 12.0, 12.0]) - this artifact's own declared critical_parameter, the most seductive axis in the wave because the ladder is already written and looks like a promoted family waiting to be declared. Refused on three counts. (1) It is a set of CLOCK READINGS: capture_config_sweep fires at ~1.45 s and the earliest freeze is 7.5 s, so at the shutter not ONE of the four has fired; a sweep of it today publishes four tiles of four bodies at the same moment of the same fall. (2) Compressed into the window by a fixture it would photograph four TRANSIENTS, each frozen by a Timer whose timeout lands on whichever physics tick the frame rate happened to produce - two runs would freeze two different crumples and the bite number would be a fact about the frame clock. (3) Recorded, not fixed here: two of the four shipped values are IDENTICAL (12.0, 12.0), so the four-stop demo already collapses two of its four samples into one, which is exactly what its own @identity warns against ('set them equal and difference collapses into repetition'). Also declined: `spacing` (composition, not material) and `show_timers` (a UI toggle, and ui_labels is never populated so it currently toggles nothing).
dna.fixture_why: AS SHIPPED ON THE BENCH THE ARTIFACT IS NOT IN FRAME AT ALL, and that is the most important thing this promotion found. capture_config_sweep._stage_default builds two DirectionalLight3Ds and a Camera3D and nothing else; the showcase profile's ground is a MeshInstance3D with no collider (_stage_showcase, ShowGround); dna.host builds a MultiMeshInstance3D with no collider (_build_host). There is NO physics floor anywhere on the bench. The four SoftBody3D spheres are released at y=3 and fall forever - the union-AABB pre-pass measures a SEPARATE probe instance at 0.35 s (about 0.6 m down) and frees it, and the photographed instance is a fresh one that lives about 1.2 s before the shutter (SETTLE 1.1 + two process frames + 0.1), roughly 7 m down, so every tile of any softbodies sweep run today is empty sky and would be reported INERT: a verdict about the harness, in the exact shape the corpus has been wrong five times out of seven. bench_floor_y 0.0 builds a StaticBody3D plane on collision_layer 1 - the layer softbody3d.gd._setup_physics sets and masks - which is the fixture supplying what a map supplies, and is what dna.fixture is for. TRAP, and it decides the number 1.35: softbody3d.gd._setup_physics contains `if global_position.y < 1.0: global_position.y = 2.0`, so ANY drop_height below 1.0 is silently overridden to 2.0 and the fixture would appear to have been ignored. 1.35 clears it with 0.35 m to spare. spacing 2.0 (from the shipped 3.0) tightens the 2x2 grid so four cells fit one frame at a distance where each body is still legible. body_damping 0.45 against softbody3d.gd's own 0.01 is what buys a SETTLED pose inside the capture window instead of a transient - see determinism.
dna.harness_note: SECOND HARNESS FACT, fixed by the same fixture and worth stating separately because it would survive a floor. Godot's SoftBody3D goes TOP-LEVEL with an identity transform on its first transform notification (it pushes the global transform to the physics server and simulates vertices in world space), so all four bodies report the same static 1 m SphereMesh AABB at the origin no matter where they actually are. _subtree_aabb counts MeshInstance3D - which SoftBody3D is - so the union box would be one 1 m cube at the origin and the camera would frame one cell of four. The bench floor slab is sized to spacing + 2.2 for exactly this reason: it is the only node in the subtree whose AABB tracks the 2x2 layout, so it doubles as the framing anchor and no separate layers=0 anchor is needed. The conclusion does not depend on which way the engine goes here: if Godot DOES republish a soft body's AABB in world space as it deforms, the 4.2 m slab still dominates the union and still frames all four cells - the slab makes the framing indifferent to the fall, which is also why the camera lands identically for all four variants. It is built ONLY under the fixture guard, so no map placement gains a node. Registry measurements.aabb_size is [0,0,0] for this token, which is consistent with both faults and was not measured against.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: pan vs cone. Both drive the body upward and narrow it - pan with two walls, cone with one point. Arithmetic: both raise the body's centroid by roughly the same 0.18 m and narrow its width from 1.0 m to ~0.72 m, so the outer silhouettes agree to within ~0.06 m on a body that is ~13% of frame width in a 2x2 grid at spacing 2.0; the visible difference is the tray's own two walls (0.70 x 0.35 m each, x4 cells) plus the crease geometry, so about 4% of frame and focus around 16%. Written down BEFORE the capture so that whichever way it lands the number is a fact rather than a fault. IF pan comes back within 1% of floor, the tray is too wide and the sphere is resting inside it untouched - narrow PAN_INNER_SPAN to 0.55 rather than blaming the axis. IF rail and cone collapse together, the bar is too thin to fold over and RAIL_TOP is too low; raise it before declaring anything.
dna.determinism: ZERO RNG in fourstopsoftbody.gd and zero in softbody3d.gd - no randf, no randi, no `seed = randi()`, nothing to seed. Two wall-clock reads exist in softbody3d.gd (_apply_idle_behavior nudges target_color by sin/cos of Time.get_unix_time_from_system) and they are visually INERT: that colour system is self-declared 'simplified, no material dependency', nothing ever writes current_color to a material, and the bodies render through the pinktartan ShaderMaterial override. The same function's pressure_coefficient line lerps 0.2 toward 0.2 in the only call that happens inside the window, and the next state change is scheduled at t=3.0 s, well after the shutter. SETTLING, which is the real question: 1.35 minus the 0.5 m sphere radius is a 0.85 m fall, contact at ~0.42 s under standard gravity, leaving about 0.78 s of settling at damping_coefficient 0.45 (against the shipped 0.01) onto a rigid obstruction - an attracting rest, not a transient. The pan, rail and cone values contact EARLIER than floor (their surfaces are 0.35 / 0.55 / 0.30 m up), so floor is the worst case and it is the one to check. THE SHUTTER IS AT ~1.2 s, NOT 1.45: read from capture_config_sweep, the photographed instance gets SETTLE (1.1) plus two process frames plus 0.1, while the 0.35 s AABB pre-pass runs on a separate probe instance that is queue_free()d before the render loop starts. So the settling margin is 0.78 s, not the 1.0 s a summed clock suggests - the least margin of the six artifacts in this wave, and the reason this is the one to verify by running the sweep twice and differencing the DEFAULT tile before trusting any number from it. RESIDUAL RISK I could not close by reading: each body is a default SphereMesh of ~2100 vertices at simulation_precision 7, four of them; if that overruns the headless frame budget Godot clamps physics steps per frame and SIMULATED time falls behind the wall clock create_timer is counting, so the pose at the shutter would become a fact about the machine. That is the accumulated-physics-steps failure in its purest form, and the two-run diff is what detects it. If the runs differ, raise body_damping before touching the axis. Once at rest a +/-1 physics tick from frame-time accumulation is invisible, which is the entire reason rest is the pin and a timed freeze was declined. The four stop timers never fire inside the window, so the axis is measured on four bodies in the same state, which is what makes the four cells comparable. softbody3d.gd._validate_physics (`if global_position.y < -0.5: global_position.y = 1.0`) cannot fire under the fixture either way: with the floor present the bodies rest near y=0.5, and the node's own transform is identity once the body goes top-level.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`. It now reads landing plus the four fixture keys, builds a signature of every value the build consumes (_signature: landing, spacing, drop_height, bench_floor_y, body_damping) and RETURNS when it has not moved. _ready records that same signature BEFORE the first build, so a deferred grid call arriving after _ready with the same values returns without touching anything. A call that arrives BEFORE _ready sets the properties and returns on is_node_ready(), because at that moment the properties ARE the build inputs and building would build twice. _rebuild frees only _owned - the nodes this script created - with remove_child before queue_free, so freed nodes cannot collide with the new ones over a name or linger a frame in the physics space. The scene's own Camera3D has an owner and is never in _owned. Nothing in the build path is deferred.
dna.scene_note: fourstopsoftbody.tscn's ROOT carries the script (verified, ext_resource id 1_n6pjx, uid cf4xfrh0d1qnn matching fourstopsoftbody.gd.uid) and also holds a bare Camera3D child, which capture_config_sweep._suppress_chrome and GridInteractablesComponent._suppress_embedded_chrome both stand down. Not a bug. The instanced softbodybody.tscn resolves by uid bw75lrwfiq6g4 and its path hint is current.

entry.description: soft_mushroom

dna.default: flesh=soft, occurrence=scattered - soft returns the shipped linear_stiffness 0.2 / damping 0.05 / pressure 0.5 value for value, and scattered draws the SAME two randf_range calls in the same order off the same global generator (rng_seed defaults to 0, which leaves the seeded generator null). The 10 map placements grow the garden they always grew.
dna.was: three unnamed SoftBody3D numbers and a for-loop over randf_range. The @identity truth says 'a mushroom cap does not decide its shape - the pin constraint, gravity and whatever bumps into it negotiate the form', and the tissue doing the negotiating was hard-coded at one setting. The scatter was not a decision at all: it is what a loop does when nobody asks, yet it is a claim about fungal ecology - that fruiting bodies come up independently - and it is not the only one fungi make.
dna.note: flesh is a MATERIAL property, not a time-domain one, but the sweep photographs at 1.1 s and a SoftBody3D at stiffness 0.05 with damping 0.05 is still moving then. The four values will differ in the frame - turgid holds a ball while slack has already collapsed - but the picture is a snapshot of a negotiation in progress, not four rest states. Deterministic under the fixture's seed, so the comparison is fair; it is simply earlier than rest. occurrence is a positional axis and is at rest immediately.
dna.fixture_note: rng_seed and spawn_span are bench knobs added for this, both defaulting to 0 = 'as shipped'. Without a seed, fifteen unseeded randf_range draws per variant make five variants five different gardens and the sweep measures noise - the documented failure for any generative artifact. Without spawn_span the field is the measured 19.45 x 20.07 m, which puts a 2 m cap at roughly 26 px in a 760 px frame: the caps become specks and an axis about cap SHAPE cannot be read at all.
dna.open: spatial_needs.footprint_cells is 9 while measured_footprint_cells is 420 - the registry books this 20 m field as a 3x3 prop. Not touched here; recorded so it is not lost.

entry.name: Breathing Room
entry.description: A corridor with soft body walls that rhythmically expand and contract.

dna.default: substance=solid, aperture=ajar - both are strict no-ops. `solid` returns from _apply_substance() before a StandardMaterial3D is constructed, so material_override stays unassigned and the slabs keep Godot's default grey; `ajar` returns from _apply_aperture() before either transform is read, so the authored x = -2.3185759 and x = +3.5541987 are untouched. All twelve appearances render exactly as before: the 5 grid tokens (SoftBodies_Obsticals, _p1, _p2, _p3, Corridor_SoftBodies_Obsticals), the 6 exhibit_furniture#mount:breathing_room slots in Trial_castelvecchio / grande / kanazawa / sainsbury / uffizi / wfc_softbodies, and the Curation_Bay_softbodies_0 roster. None carries a #substance: or #aperture: token, and a bare token leaves merged_config empty so apply_grid_config is never called at all.
dna.was: the .tscn root carried NO SCRIPT - two hand-authored SoftBody3D slabs with baked pinned points, no material override, and no breathing. The sinusoidal pressure loop the description promises lives in the sibling breathing_room.gd, which nothing in the repository loads.
dna.declined: breath_speed and breath_amplitude, the orphan script's named critical_parameter. They modulate pressure_coefficient over time, the evidence here is one still per value, and soft bodies are still settling at the 1.1 s capture settle - sweeping them would photograph the settle, not the axis.
dna.note: aperture is applied in _enter_tree, before the SoftBody3D children enter the tree and pin their empty-path attachments to world space. A value arriving later through apply_grid_config can still change substance but cannot move a live soft body.

dna.default: crimp=swell, heading=none. `swell` returns the literal 0.25 that the shipped `var wave_offset := i * 0.25` already multiplied i by, so the line is now `float(i) * gradient` computing the same IEEE product. `none` sets `shaped = false` and the envelope multiply is never reached, so `xform.origin.z = base_wave + wind_noise` stands character for character as it shipped. The two determinism exports are no-ops at their defaults too: `frozen_phase` -1.0 fails its `>= 0.0` test so t is `float(Time.get_ticks_msec()) * 0.001 + time_offset` as before, and `wave_seed` -1 returns from setup_joyful_animation() on the shipped `time_offset = randf() * TAU` - the same single draw off the same global generator, in the same order, so even the RNG stream is untouched. THIRTEEN appearances, each read out of its map JSON for this pass, and NOT ONE of them carries a `#key:value` tail: five grid tokens (SoftBodies_Obsticals as `flagdancer:90`, and SoftBodies_Obsticals_p1 / _p2 / _p3 / Corridor_SoftBodies_Obsticals as the bare word - a rotation suffix is not a config, so merged_config is empty and apply_grid_config is never called), seven `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:flagdancer` mounts (Trial_castelvecchio / grande / kanazawa / lattice_pm_17 / sainsbury / uffizi / wfc_softbodies), and the Curation_Bay_softbodies_0 curation_station roster. Were a host to forward its own keys anyway, apply_grid_config reads only the four it declares, so the signature is unchanged and it returns before assigning anything.
dna.was: one hard-coded wave, and no held edge at all. `i * 0.25` fixed the spatial period at two thirds of a wave across six metres for every flag in the project, and every bone got the SAME amplitude (0.4 and 0.15) because `progress` entered the noise's PHASE and never its ENVELOPE - so the shipped object is a sheet floating free in space, undulating exactly as much at one end as the other. The maps have been describing something else for months: SoftBodies_Obsticals/critical.md says the flag is 'pinned at one edge - attached, constrained, unable to leave its pole', and technical.md says 'A cloth surface pinned along one edge'. No line of code ever pinned an edge. `heading=hoist` is the value that makes this artifact do what its own documentation has been claiming it does.
dna.note: `crimp` is NEW and free corpus-wide - the textile word for the wave standing in a fabric. Not `fold` (polyhedron_nets_cube: whether a net is folded, a discrete state); not `swell` (marching_cubes: terrain amplitude class); not `weave` (ruth_asawa_sculpture: which wire topology gets emitted, a construction, where crimp is a deformation of one fixed construction). `heading` is NEW - the vexillological and curtain-making name for the reinforced edge a cloth is attached by. Deliberately NOT `suspension` (cloth_straps, spring_system): that axis names the FURNITURE a hanging body hangs from and builds a rank of steel around an untouched cloth. This one builds nothing and moves no prop; it changes which part of the cloth is allowed to move. Not `anchorage` (ant_colony_v2, nest-site arrangement), not `hang` (gallery_winner_showcase, the arrangement of hung objects), not `attach` (point: float/stake/plate). Both axes were chosen for the only property of a wave that survives being frozen - its SHAPE ALONG THE CLOTH - because everything in this sequence moves and the evidence is one still.
dna.declined: `wind_strength` (1.0), the @identity's own declared critical_parameter and the most tempting knob in the file. Refused because at a frozen phase it is nothing but a uniform amplitude multiplier on a sine: four values are four SCALINGS of one shape, which the union-AABB camera then partly divides back out again, and in motion it reads as speed-of-flapping rather than as form. `celebration_intensity` is worse - it is consulted only while `celebration_mode` is true, and celebration_mode can only be turned on by a live ui_accept press that no capture will ever make, so all four values would render byte-identically. Also declined: the sine frequencies 2.0, 3.7 and 0.8, which are pure rates - one photograph each of an arbitrary instant.
dna.placements: 13 appearances, 0 configured: 5 grid tokens + 7 exhibit_furniture mounts + 1 curation_station roster. None carries a config tail, so none reaches the new code.
dna.fixture_why: AS SHIPPED THERE IS NO DETERMINISM HERE, TWICE OVER, and 'has it settled by 1.45 s' is not even the right question: there is no simulation to settle. The pose is a closed-form function of `t = Time.get_ticks_msec() * 0.001 + time_offset`, so the flag is never at rest and the shutter photographs the wall clock; and `time_offset = randf() * TAU` is drawn off the global generator with no seed, which is five different objects across five variants. (The file LOOKS like it seeds something - `var noise_seed := int(time_offset * 1000) % 1000` - and that local is never read again. Decoration, not a seed. The second random draw the brief warns about, `randf_range(0.8, 1.2)`, is inside create_flag_parade(), which nothing in the repository calls.) frozen_phase 2.35 makes t a constant, so time_offset is never read, the flag is MOTIONLESS, and the picture is a pure function of the exports on every machine. 2.35 rather than a round number because it gives a well-spread wave at the default - bone 0 at sin(4.70) = -1.000, bone 8 at sin(6.70) = +0.405, bone 16 at sin(8.70) = +0.666, all times 0.4 - where a near-flat instant would flatter every value equally. wave_seed 20260812 is for the WORLD, not the bench: in a live map the phase must keep running, and an explicit integer (never `rng.seed = randi()`, which is the opposite of seeding) makes it the same flag on every launch. Both are written as NUMBERS, not strings, because they are assigned straight onto typed float and int exports before _ready.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config checks each word against CRIMPS / HEADINGS, builds a signature of all four values, and RETURNS before assigning anything when it equals `_config_sig` - which _ready() primes with the shipped values, so a call carrying keys this artifact does not declare is a strict no-op. Nothing rebuilds geometry in any case: all four values are read fresh by _process every frame, so a live placement changes shape without a single node being freed. setup_joyful_animation() re-runs only when the seed itself moved, so a config repeating the shipped -1 never spends a second randf() and never re-rolls a running flag. _ready() builds synchronously and there is no call_deferred in the build path. Teardown now frees an `_owned` array (skeleton, mesh, particles) instead of the shipped `for child in get_children(): if not child.owner: child.queue_free()`, which took down every node any other system had parented to this artifact at runtime.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, and it disagrees with the design on BOTH axes, which is the only kind of prediction worth writing. Method: the sheet carries no material (see `finding`), so its interior is uniform and only the SILHOUETTE can differ; project each of the 17 bone columns with the canonical rig (world +Z maps to (-0.581, -0.209) screen metres at yaw 0.62 / pitch -0.26), rasterise the union of the 16 quads between columns, and take the symmetric difference. crimp: the design named ripple vs corrugation. WRONG - that pair is FOURTH of six. The closest is flat vs corrugation at 0.69% of the full frame (6.8% of the subject crop, ~2.3% critic frame), because at 1.2 rad per bone corrugation's wave averages out over the silhouette and its end column lands near where flat's does; ripple vs corrugation is 1.41% (~4.6% critic frame), a factor of 2.0 wider. Structural note the design missed: bone 0 has wave_offset = 0 * gradient = 0 for EVERY value, so all four crimp tiles share their left edge exactly and the difference grows linearly toward bone 16. heading: the design named hoist vs fly as the closest and the likeliest to miss the bar. It is the WIDEST of the six - 0.90% of frame at the swept default crimp=swell (2.9% critic frame). The closest is hoist vs both at 0.42% (4.1% of crop, ~1.4% critic frame), because the `both` bunting envelope and the `hoist` ramp agree at the dead hoist end and differ only over the fly half. On FOCUS both axes should saturate near 33% rather than separate, since every differing pixel is a full-contrast sheet-versus-background flip and the differing area exceeds the hottest-5% window: on a silhouette-only subject FOCUS IS THE WRONG DISCRIMINATOR and `frame` is the informative number. ALL OF THIS IS CONDITIONAL - see `finding`. The design also assumed the flag fills ~60% of frame; it is 9.5% at framing 1.0, a factor of 6.3, which is why every predicted percentage here is smaller than the design's.
dna.finding: DO NOT SWEEP THIS TOKEN YET - IT PHOTOGRAPHS AS A WHITE QUAD, AND THE AXES ARE NOT THE REASON. The only capture that exists (user://multi_shots/flagdancer, 2026-04-20, four angles) shows a single small white quadrilateral and no flag from any angle, and no commit has touched this folder since, so it is current. That quad is the .tscn's own vestigial 1x1 QuadMesh; the procedural 6x4 m flag is in the AABB and not in the picture - the camera had pulled back to about 15 m of framed extent, which is the 7.2 m mesh diagonal times the capturer's pad, so the mesh resource exists and draws nothing. Cause, read out of the code: create_pride_flag_with_bones() assigns `skinned_mesh.skeleton = skeleton.get_path()` immediately after add_child, when the Skeleton3D still has ZERO bones and before the mesh is committed. Godot resolves that path at assignment and, with no explicit Skin, caches an auto-skin built from the rest transforms of nothing; the 17 bones added afterwards never regenerate it, so the surface is skinned against an empty bind array. Two working procedural skinned meshes in this repository do the opposite in both respects - commons/artifacts/ik_arm_demo (explicit Skin, bind poses set from `skeleton.get_bone_rest(i).affine_inverse()`, `skeleton` assigned LAST) and commons/hazards/octapod_crawler/one_leg (explicit Skin, MeshInstance3D parented UNDER the Skeleton3D). SECOND defect on the same mesh: st.commit() is assigned with no material and SurfaceTool sets none, so the default StandardMaterial3D renders it white with `vertex_color_use_as_albedo` off - every stripe colour in flag_colors is written into the mesh as vertex colour and then never shown. A pride flag that renders white. NEITHER IS FIXED IN THIS PASS, deliberately: both change what all 13 shipped placements look like, both are unverifiable without a Godot run, and this pass was forbidden one. The axes, the defaults and the fixture are complete and correct behind them.
dna.measurement_risk: Even once it renders, the subject is only 9.5% of frame at framing 1.0 - the AABB is 6 x 4 x ~0, a wide flat sheet, and PAD 1.9 on the DIAGONAL wastes most of the frame. A `dna.framing` near 0.62 would put it at ~25% and roughly triple every frame number above; it is deliberately NOT set here, because tuning a framing value against a subject that has never been photographed would be a guess wearing the clothes of a measurement. Set it in the same pass that repairs the render, and measure. Second risk: the sheet's normals are all +Z and the bone bases carry no rotation, so shading cannot vary across the surface - with or without a material the axes live in the silhouette and in the stripe boundaries, never in shading.

entry.description: Generate reaction-diffusion Turing patterns in real-time — spots, stripes, and labyrinthine structures emerge from the interplay of activator and inhibitor chemicals diffusing at different rates. Alan Turing's morphogenesis made visible.

dna.framing_why: MEASURED, and it is the whole story rather than a polish pass. The update rule was ported to numpy and the six regimes compared ON THE TEXTURE at the fixture (resolution 40, 1600 steps): spots vs coral changes 15-21% of the pattern cells and stripes vs coral changes 93%. The sweep reported 0.497% and 2.089%. The ratio is the frame - the pattern is a 1 x 1 m quad lying FLAT and photographed from 14.9 degrees above the horizon, so it presents 0.257 of its own area, and the union box is stretched to a 1.68 m diagonal by the VR control panel at z=0.65 and the framed info plate at z=-0.58. 2.7% of frame times 20% of the pattern is 0.54%, which reproduces the measurement to within a tenth of a percent: the axis was never weak, the camera was 5.2 m away. 0.6 is set against a computed clipping limit - the widest screen extent is the far corner of the base plate at 0.765 m, so the camera cannot come closer than 0.48, and 0.6 keeps a quarter of the frame as margin while multiplying every measured area by 2.78. Uniform scale is not an alternative: display_size scales the AABB with the artifact, so the camera pulls back by the same factor and nothing is gained.
dna.fixture_why: MANDATORY, three separate reasons, and all three default to shipped behaviour in code so none of them is an axis. pattern_seed pins the five seeded blobs - _seed_random draws them with the global randi_range, so six regime frames would be six different inoculations and the bite number would measure the RNG, not the feed/kill pair (the generative-artifact trap). warmup runs the chemistry before the first frame: at the shipped 4 steps per frame a 0.35 s settle reaches step 84 and all six values photograph the same five undifferentiated blobs. resolution 40 rather than the shipped 64 is a TIME budget, not a look - this is an interpreted CPU Gray-Scott loop and 1600 steps at 64x64 is 6.5 M cell updates inside _ready, which blocks the boot past the capture watchdog; the code caps it at 4 M regardless of what a fixture asks for.
dna.fixture_ladder: Measured, not assumed. The update rule was re-implemented exactly (same 0.2/0.05 laplacian weights, same clamp, same 5-disc seeding) and run per preset at 32/40/48/64 cells and 300-6000 steps. The six regimes are indistinguishable below ~800 steps and fully settled by ~2000; at resolution 40 / 1600 steps the V-coverage reads spots 0.06, stripes 0.21, maze 0.16, mitosis 0.07, coral 0.03, waves 0.13, and every pair differs by at least 0.04 mean |dV| per cell (most by over 0.11). Two facts worth knowing before reading the sheet: at the shipped seeding (U=0.5, V=0.25 in five discs) the Coral preset very nearly dies out - it settles at 3% coverage - and the Spots preset stabilises as a handful of isolated dots rather than filling the field. Those are facts about the presets, not about the capture.
dna.deepened: 2026-08-05, two moves, and the first one is a correction of the verdict rather than of the artifact. (1) dna.framing 0.6. The regime axis is not close to weak: ported to numpy at the fixture settings, the six presets differ by 15% (spots vs coral, the reported worst pair) to 93% (stripes vs coral) OF THE PATTERN CELLS. The sweep saw 0.497% and 2.089% because the pattern surface is only about 2.7% of the frame, and 2.7% x 20% = 0.54% reproduces the reported number almost exactly. A flat 1 m plate seen from 14.9 degrees shows a quarter of its area, and a control panel 0.65 m away in +z and a framed info plate 0.58 m away in -z stretch the fitted diagonal to 1.68 m. Nothing about the chemistry needed changing. (2) A SECOND AXIS, `seeding`, which is the argument this file's own truth line makes and no knob could reach: 'pattern emerges from the ratio of two diffusion rates - not from a template, not from a gene'. regime moves feed and kill; the truth sentence is about neither, and every placement in the corpus has started from the same five random discs since the artifact was written. The four values were chosen by measurement, not taste - all four run at all six regimes, and the value list is what survived: `noise` was tried at five densities from 0.08 to 0.8 and no density ignites more than two regimes, so it was dropped rather than shipped as four blank tiles; `band` was dropped because under mitosis it and `ring` both die to an empty field, which is two values showing one picture, the twin fault the critic exists to catch. THE RESULT IS TWO-SIDED, which is why it is worth having: under `maze` the four seedings settle at coverage 0.434 / 0.410 / 0.443 / 0.440 while 39-73% of the CELLS differ - the law fixes how much, the seed fixes where, and the truth line holds. Under `waves` the lattice never ignites and under `mitosis` the ring dies out, so the seed also decides IF there is a pattern at all. Minimum pairwise texture difference across all six regimes is 9.7% and the median is around 45%, comparable to regime's own spread. NOT MEASURED YET: 6 x 4 is 24 variants and build_dna_gallery's default cap is 9, which keeps the first axis that fits and silently drops the second - this needs --max=24. Worth knowing regardless: the last sweep of `regime` only rendered FIVE values. Cap trimming drops from the END of the list, so `waves` - the preset furthest from the others in the phase space, at f=0.014 / k=0.047 - is the one value that has never been photographed.
dna.default: regime=spots, seeding=discs - both no-ops. _seed_discs is the shipped inoculation moved into a named function and not otherwise touched: the same five discs, the same random centres and radii, drawn in the same order and the same count from the same generator, so an existing placement is inoculated byte for byte as before. apply_grid_config pulls `seeding` out of the blanket write-through loop for the same reason it pulls `regime` - writing the word alone would change what the RESET button draws next while leaving the field on screen inoculated the old way, so the artifact would be labelled one thing and showing another - and it re-seeds only when the word validates against SEEDINGS, DIFFERS from the one held, and _ready has already built the grids. None of the 14 rooms sends either key. AND, unchanged from the promotion: regime=spots - spots is PRESETS[0], which is f=0.055 / k=0.062, which is the pattern_type the .tscn has always written on the root. _resolve_regime assigns pattern_type ONLY when the resolved index differs, so at the default not one byte is written and the setter never fires; _ready is otherwise the same six calls in the same order. pattern_seed and warmup both default to 0, which is the shipped fresh-every-launch inoculation and no pre-run at all, so a player still meets the blank field and watches it organise. apply_grid_config keeps its legacy write-through loop untouched and handles regime separately, guarded on the word being one PRESETS builds and on it differing; neither of the two curation bays nor the five museum trials that mount this artifact sends it, so all 14 rooms are unchanged.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, and the axis was already sitting in the source. The six-point phase space was an @export_enum INT called pattern_type with a working setter and a VR slider wired to it, and the registry had never been told. Worse, the integer was unreachable from a map token even by hand: map_data.json config values arrive as STRINGS and apply_grid_config's whole body was a blanket `if key in self: set(key, ...)`, so 'turing_pattern_generator#pattern_type:2' tried to write "2" into a typed int, was rejected, and silently rendered Spots. Fourteen placements, one regime.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-04, the lsystem_editor case again. regime is the corpus's word for 'which named case of this system's parameter space is in force' (harmonic_motion_demo, mass_spring_damper, bouncing_ball, bifurcation_diagram) and the values are DERIVED from PRESETS - _regime_index reads the third column of the table, so the declared list cannot drift from the code the way science_screen's did. The axis is deliberately the named regime and NOT feed or kill as continuous floats: this loop's evidence is one still per value, a slider position is not a claim, and the whole teaching point of the @identity ('each preset is a point in that space') is that the interesting structure is a handful of named islands. CAUTION ON RECORD: reaction_diffusion, the GPU sibling this file's @identity names, was measured GENUINELY INERT - 62% of frame and 15 grey levels. That verdict was about a continuous parameter on an unwarmed field; the regimes here differ by a factor of seven in coverage once the chemistry has actually run.
